items.impact: Approval is bound to durable CAS, PlanApproved, and PlanCompileRun effects, preventing a GUI-only success state from serving as implementation evidence.
items.statement: Approve And Build has an explicit production command, handler, enabled and disabled selectors, durable approval effects, accessibility semantics, and a regression-evidence requirement.
items.title: Final approval has a durable production-wiring contract

items.impact: READY-looking compile and manifest pills could mislead users and exclude keyboard users if promoted without a real state contract and semantic-control replacement.
items.statement: The compile-state and handoff-manifest READY pills are click-only custom targets explicitly marked as concept fixtures, so their displayed readiness is not acceptable state or accessibility evidence.
items.title: READY pills are non-authoritative and lack keyboard parity

items.impact: The route can be tested against explicit target and correlation identity instead of relying on label text or implicit tab state.
items.statement: Open Plan Compile is a route-only production command with explicit target surface, target tab, optional run identities, source surface, correlation id, disabled reasons, and a route receipt requirement.
items.title: Plan Compile routing is identity-bound

items.impact: Multiple non-selected tabs can remain in the tab order, undermining a predictable roving-tabindex model and allowing focus semantics to diverge from selected state.
items.statement: The inactive Node Graph tab is declared aria-selected false while retaining tabindex 0; the same pattern appears on other inactive orchestrator tabs and lacks a production focus-transition oracle.
items.title: Inactive orchestrator tabs expose inconsistent focus state

evidence.exact_quote: "payload_contract": "hitl_request_id, step_id or blocked_sequence, attempt_id, approval_scope_key, actor_ref, correlation_id"

items.impact: A HITL approval is scoped to one current request and cannot silently become authority to launch a second ordinary build.
items.statement: Approve Step is explicitly constrained to scoped HITL recovery, with request, step or blocked-sequence, attempt, scope, actor, and correlation identities plus stale, wrong-scope, disabled, and already-resolved rejection states.
items.title: HITL approval authority is narrowly scoped

evidence.exact_quote:

        "No production command is assigned in this repair; remains concept lineage until an owner doc promotes it and adds command/state/handler/receipt/test evidence.",

items.impact: Running and Done labels, counts, and hierarchy can appear operational even though no production selector, event source, freshness rule, or receipt proves them.
items.statement: The Plan Compile hierarchy presents production-looking progress states but is intentionally unpromoted concept lineage, leaving its state producer, stale-data behavior, consumers, and acceptance evidence unresolved in the canonical owners.
items.title: Plan Compile progress can overstate runtime truth

evidence.exact_quote: "owner_rationale": "Owner-adjudicated as concept/source-lineage only. This control is not production evidence and is not promoted until a canonical owner doc accepts the behavior and a production wiring row supplies command/state/receipt/test evidence."

items.impact: The source correctly prevents graph placeholders, sample run identities, and visual state from being mistaken for production implementation evidence.
items.statement: The Node Graph surface and all of its layout, zoom, fit, filter, search, and visibility controls are consistently owner-adjudicated as concept lineage rather than production evidence.
items.title: Node Graph concept status is explicit

items.impact: Promoting the control without an owner contract could duplicate runs, start against stale planning state, or show a run before durable creation succeeds.
items.statement: Start Run is a high-authority operation with no command, payload, authorization, idempotency, concurrent-start, partial-creation, rollback, receipt, or disabled-state contract in this control inventory.
items.title: Start Run has no production authority contract

items.impact: The two recovery paths could replay side effects, reuse an unsafe checkpoint, orphan an old attempt, or create competing attempts without a defined authority and receipt model.
items.statement: Retry from safe point and Start fresh attempt are distinct recovery operations but both remain concept-only with no safe-point identity, attempt lineage, side-effect replay policy, concurrency exclusion, rollback, or durable outcome oracle.
items.title: Node recovery controls leave replay and lineage undefined

evidence.exact_quote: "label": "Type: All TestLog Screenshot BrowserTrace FileSnapshot Metric GateReport CommandOutput",

items.impact: The concept establishes a useful observable evidence taxonomy and filter affordance while correctly withholding production status.
items.statement: The Evidence surface concept exposes a typed evidence catalog spanning logs, screenshots, browser traces, file snapshots, metrics, gate reports, and command output, with type filtering and search.
items.title: Evidence browsing has a concrete concept taxonomy

items.impact: An implementation could irreversibly remove run history or linked evidence without authorization, confirmation, retention enforcement, cascade visibility, concurrency control, or a recovery record.
items.statement: Delete Run is presented as a history action but remains concept-only and has no target identity, authorization, confirmation, retention, evidence-cascade, concurrent-run, tombstone, undo, or deletion-receipt contract.
items.title: Delete Run lacks destructive-action safeguards

items.impact: Evidence may contain logs, screenshots, traces, snapshots, or command output; an unconstrained export could disclose secrets or personal data, exceed memory limits, or produce incomplete files under partial failure.
items.statement: Evidence Export, Copy, and Open in Editor are concept-only and do not define scope, authorization, secret redaction, provenance, maximum size, streaming behavior, offline handling, partial-file cleanup, destination, or export receipt.
items.title: Evidence export has no privacy or large-payload boundary

evidence.exact_quote: "owner_rationale": "Owner-adjudicated as concept/source-lineage only. This control is not production evidence and is not promoted until a canonical owner doc accepts the behavior and a production wiring row supplies command/state/receipt/test evidence."

items.impact: CSV and JSON output can diverge in schema, filtering, redaction, precision, and completeness, making exported cost and activity data unsafe or non-reproducible.
items.statement: The orchestrator ledger offers CSV and JSON export but both controls remain concept-only, with no filter-snapshot, schema-version, redaction, precision, pagination, maximum-size, destination, partial-failure, or completion-receipt contract.
items.title: Usage-ledger exports are not contractually reproducible

items.impact: The selected Overview tab can be rendered, but there is no promoted navigation command, route state, deep-link behavior, or state-restoration oracle tying that visual selection to an authoritative page projection.
items.statement: The first Usage tab exposes selected GUI state, yet all Usage tabs are concept-only and do not identify the navigation owner, route payload, selected-state producer, restoration behavior, or callers and consumers.
items.title: Usage tab selection lacks authoritative navigation state

items.impact: The concept communicates two useful time-window families but leaves their production query semantics to the canonical Usage owner.
items.statement: Usage exposes a Session, Today, 7d, and 30d period selector plus a second 1h, 5h, 24h, 7d, and 30d time-window selector, all explicitly retained as concept lineage.
items.title: Usage concept defines two time-window selector families

items.impact: A refresh spanning providers, analytics, ledger, and overview data could mix snapshots, overwrite newer results, hide provider failures, or leave the GUI looking current while offline or partially stale.
items.statement: Refresh all usage data is concept-only and lacks snapshot identity, freshness timestamp, concurrent-refresh policy, provider fan-out and timeout behavior, cancellation, partial-success representation, offline behavior, stale-result suppression, and completion receipt.
items.title: Usage refresh has no coherent-snapshot or partial-failure contract

items.impact: Switching between organization and personal billing context without atomic authority and cache-isolation rules could leak usage data, attribute costs to the wrong account, or retain stale account projections.
items.statement: The billing selector and Switch Account control remain concept-only and do not define actor authority, target account identity, reauthentication, tenant isolation, unsaved work, in-flight query cancellation, cache invalidation, atomic projection replacement, rollback, or audit receipt.
items.title: Account switching lacks tenant-isolation and atomicity rules

evidence.exact_quote: "owner_rationale": "Owner-adjudicated as concept/source-lineage only. This control is not production evidence and is not promoted until a canonical owner doc accepts the behavior and a production wiring row supplies command/state/receipt/test evidence."

items.impact: An ambiguous retry could duplicate provider requests, retry successful subrequests, act on a stale account or time window, or replace a newer successful projection with an older response.
items.statement: The Usage Retry control is concept-only and does not identify the failed operation, provider subset, account, query window, attempt, idempotency key, backoff, cancellation, stale-response guard, or durable retry outcome.
items.title: Usage Retry has no scoped recovery contract

segments.summary: Reviewed all wizard final-review, compile-state pill, activity, and initial orchestrator-tab controls; extracted the durable approval contract and the non-authoritative READY-pill accessibility seam.
Reviewed all remaining orchestrator tabs, status panel, Plan Compile route, run controls, Open Build contract, and status link; extracted route identity and the inactive-tab focus inconsistency.

Reviewed scoped HITL approval, reject and clear controls, Plan Compile hierarchy, expansion and state filters, and all hierarchy nodes; extracted the narrow approval authority and progress-truth seam.

Reviewed the remainder of the Plan Compile tree and the complete Node Graph placeholder, start, layout, zoom, fit, filter, search, visibility, and quick-filter inventory; distinguished explicit concept status from the missing Start Run authority contract.

Reviewed all remaining graph quick filters, node detail sections, plan and log links, recovery actions, reset control, and the Evidence panel and filters; extracted the recovery-lineage gap and evidence taxonomy.

Reviewed evidence detail actions, run history and deletion, ledger filters and navigation, CSV and JSON exports, and the first Usage tab; extracted destructive deletion and evidence-export privacy gaps.

Reviewed the complete Usage tab strip, top-level refresh and export, period selectors, time-window selectors, and trailing usage actions; extracted export reproducibility and tab-selection authority gaps.

Reviewed all repeated Usage refresh and analytics actions, billing account selection and switch history, Switch Account, and terminal Retry controls; extracted time-window intent plus refresh, tenant isolation, and scoped-retry gaps.

How are PlanCompileRun, runtime HITL, orchestrator run, evidence, usage ledger, and billing-account identities propagated without permitting stale cross-surface actions?
